title: The variance of a sum of m identically-distributed uncorrelated trials is m*q(1-q), and it is at the rationals because the record has no mulComm
statement: Let X be a family of rational-valued random variables on a finite index range [0, n) with a distribution p, let m be a natural number and q a rational. If the family is pairwise uncorrelated below m and every trial below m has variance q(1-q), then the pointwise sum of the first m trials has variance m*q(1-q). Both extra hypotheses are exactly the ones Rat.variance_sumVars carries and no more. The proof is the same two steps as the mean, over Rat.variance_sumVars instead of Rat.expectation_sumVars. The statement lives at the rationals rather than over AlgS.OrderedRing for a MEASURED reason: the generic variance is the centred form and the generic covariance the computational one, and relating them needs E[fun k => X k * c] ~ E[X]*c, which pulls a constant past the weight p k and therefore needs mulComm -- a field ADR-1592 deliberately withheld. So the generic shelf has no variance_eq, hence no variance_add_of_uncorrelated, hence no variance of a sum. That is a fact about the RECORD, not about the mathematics: the moment AlgS.CommOrderedRing exists this theorem moves up verbatim.

formal.statement: theorem Rat.binomial_variance : forall (X : Nat -> Nat -> Rat) (p : Nat -> Rat) (n : Nat), Rat.IsDistribution p n -> forall (m : Nat) (q : Rat), Rat.PairwiseUncorrelated X m p n -> (forall j, Nat.lt j m -> Eq (Rat.variance (X j) p n) (Rat.mul q (Rat.sub Rat.one q))) -> Eq (Rat.variance (Rat.sumVars X m) p n) (Rat.mul (Rat.natDivSucc m 0) (Rat.mul q (Rat.sub Rat.one q)))

evidence.supports: The declaration is admitted by the trusted kernel gate with an empty Kernel::axiom_footprint, together with every other declaration of ADR-1631's rational binomial layer. The test asserts Environment::contains FIRST, because an absent name has an empty footprint too.
evidence.checker_command: cargo test --release -p axeyum-lean-kernel --lib rat_prelude::binomial_rat::binomial_rat_tests::binomial_rat_declarations_are_axiom_free -- --exact 2>&1 | grep -c '^test result: ok. 1 passed'
evidence.notes: grep -c, not grep -q: -q would SIGPIPE the producer under pipefail, and -c exits 1 printing 0 when the line is absent, so a suite that compiled to zero tests and exited 0 is caught rather than counted as a pass. --release is mandatory: the rational prelude SIGABRTs on the default debug thread stack.

notes: The q(1-q) shape in the hypothesis is not decoration: it is the shape both AlgS.OrderedRing.bernoulli_variance and the rational development's own Rat.variance_indicator produce, so this theorem composes with either without a rewrite. There is no independence predicate anywhere in this development and none is introduced: independence is a statement about a joint law over a product space, and with one weight function over one index range there is none, so pairwise uncorrelatedness is the honest and strictly weaker hypothesis.
